failures.text: How does an idea get from a draft all the way to paper trading with real allocated capital?
failures.answer: Sir, an idea climbs a fixed staircase, and no step is skipped. A finding is noted on the nightly card, becomes a draft once its count how often it fires (for example, the same miss on 3 of 7 sessions), and is registered only when you say yes, which writes the study down before it runs. It is then tested on 2000-2023 at a the strict pass mark, runs as a paper trial on live sessions (20 sessions needed), and must beat chance and the average stock on 10 separate sessions after costs. Only then, with a check that no future data leaked in and your yes again, may the allocated paper capital use it; nothing has reached that step yet.

problems.why: It calls the process a "staircase" and uses unexplained terms like "nightly card", "registered" and "pass mark", and the text is garbled in places ("once its count how often it fires", "at a the strict pass mark"), so a beginner would struggle to follow the pipeline.
